title: Records, structs and copies

outcomes.can: Make a changed copy of a record and predict what the original holds.
Predict == for records, structs and classes.
Read the error from assigning to a record's property.
Return a new list of changed records and leave the input list unchanged.

intro: Some types exist to carry data. This module covers records, which compare by value and are copied with with, and structs, which are copied on every assignment. It also shows how both differ from a class.

steps.title: A record carries data
steps.text: record Job(string Title, int Minutes); declares a record in one line. It has a constructor with those two parameters and a property for each. The properties can be set only when the record is created. To change something you make a copy: first with { Minutes = 45 } is a new Job with the same Title and a different Minutes. Two records are equal with == when all their values are equal. Printing a record shows its type name and values.

steps.title: Copy with a change
steps.text: second is made from first with one value changed. Predict the first line of output.

steps.title: Follow the copy
steps.text: with created a second Job and left first alone, so first.Minutes is still 30. The second line shows the copy: the same Title and the new Minutes. Nothing can change a Job after it is created, so code that holds one can rely on it.

steps.title: Value or reference
steps.text: A struct is a value type, like int. Assigning it copies the whole value, so Size b = a; gives b its own Width. A class is a reference type: assignment copies the reference and both names refer to one object. For == the rule also depends on the type. Records compare their values. Classes compare references, so two separate objects are not equal even when they hold the same data.

steps.title: Check each type
steps.text: first == new Job("Pack", 30) is True because records compare values. a.Width is 2 because b is a separate copy, so setting b.Width to 9 changed only b. boxA == boxB is False because they are two different objects, and a class compares references.

steps.title: Assign to a record's property
steps.text: Line 2 tries to change a record after it was created. Read the example before checking.

steps.title: Read the compiler error
steps.text: Check the example. CS8852 says an init-only property can be assigned only while the object is being created. Write first with { Minutes = 45 } and use the copy it produces.

choices.feedback: Size is a struct, so b is a separate copy. Changing b leaves a.Width at 2.
Records compare by value, and both have Pack and 30.
